title: Calculate Euclidean Distance
learning_objective: Learn how to translate the two-dimensional distance formula into SQL.

tutorial.explanation: The distance between two points is the square root of the squared x difference plus the squared y difference. SQL can calculate this with arithmetic, POWER, SQRT, and ROUND.
tutorial.syntax: SELECT SQRT(POWER(p1.x - p2.x, 2) + POWER(p1.y - p2.y, 2)) AS distance FROM points p1 CROSS JOIN points p2 WHERE p1.id < p2.id;
tutorial.mental_model: Treat each point pair like one row. Inside that row, calculate the x difference, y difference, square them, add them, and take the square root.

guided_example.prompt: Calculate the distance for every unique point pair.
guided_example.solution_query: SELECT p1.id AS point_a, p2.id AS point_b, SQRT(POWER(p1.x - p2.x, 2) + POWER(p1.y - p2.y, 2)) AS distance FROM points p1 CROSS JOIN points p2 WHERE p1.id < p2.id ORDER BY point_a, point_b;
guided_example.explanation: Each unique pair becomes one row, and the distance formula is calculated for that row.

practice.prompt: Return each unique point pair and its distance rounded to 2 decimals.
practice.expected_query: SELECT p1.id AS point_a, p2.id AS point_b, ROUND(SQRT(POWER(p1.x - p2.x, 2) + POWER(p1.y - p2.y, 2)), 2) AS distance FROM points p1 CROSS JOIN points p2 WHERE p1.id < p2.id ORDER BY point_a, point_b;

hints: The squared x difference is POWER(p1.x - p2.x, 2).
Keep p1.id < p2.id so each pair appears once.
